newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets 1997 stock issue quota at 30 bln yuan.
newsitem.headline: China sets 1997 stock issue quota at 30 bln yuan.

text.p: China's securities regulators have set a quota of 30 billion yuan ($3.6 billion) of new stock issues for 1997, the official Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
Xinhua said the quota had been set by the Securities Commission of the State Council and the State Planning Commission.
The figure is double the 15 billion yuan quota set for 1996.
The quota was aimed at promoting development of the national economy as well as assisting large and medium size enterprises, the news agency said.

Stock offerings under the quota would focus on the energy, transport, telecommunications and high technology sectors. They would also be heavily weighted towards the 1,000 companies designated as priority enterprises, as well as some 120 enterprise groups that have been singled out for special treatment, the news agency said.
